title: China just banned all Western AI models — what happens next

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: If China bans Western AI models, how will it reshape global innovation and trust in AI systems?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: China can develop its own models, but training them requires data, compute power, and time—resources not easily replicated overnight.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: This could deepen the digital divide, limiting access to advanced AI tools for global researchers and smaller economies.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Builders are focusing on open-source models and federated learning to ensure broader access and compliance with local regulations.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A future where AI is more inclusive, with diverse models coexisting and learning from one another across borders.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The ban may accelerate innovation, but only if collaboration and ethical frameworks keep pace with technological advances.

video_cue: A split-screen showing Chinese engineers training AI models alongside international researchers in a collaborative virtual environment.
